findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: It was observed that there are no signed employee health reporting agreements available in the facility. The PIC stated that they store them digitally and are working on getting them into a binder to keep at the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that all employees have signed an employee health reporting agreement.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: There is observed to not be a chemical that kills Norovirus available in the facility. The PIC stated that they have bleach on delivery to come tomorrow. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that there is a chemical that kills Norovirus available in the facility in case of a vomit/diarrheal event.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) had to leave at the end of the inspection and there was not another CFPM to take their place. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: It was observed that there are no signed employee health reporting agreements available in the facility. It was discussed with the PIC that all employees must sign an employee health reporting agreement and that these should be available for all future health inspections. Inspectors provided blank copies to the PIC. A follow up is scheduled for 9/17/2026 to ensure that all employees have signed an employee health reporting agreement.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: There was observed to not be a Norovirus clean up procedure available in the facility. A Norovirus cleanup policy was provided to the facility, but there is no bleach or other chemical that kills Norovirus available in the case of a vomit or diarrheal event. A follow up is scheduled for 9/17/2026 to ensure that the facility has either obtained bleach or a chemical that kills Norovirus.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was observed to be raw bacon stored on top of cooked brisket and ready-to-eat cheese in the double door cooler. CORRECTED- The cheese was moved to an upper shelf and the brisket was moved to the side so the raw bacon is no longer on top of ready-to-eat foods. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was observed to be an open bottle of Golden sauce stored on the shelf at room temperature. The bottle states to “Refrigerate After Opening”. CORRECTED- The sauce was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that staff are reading the bottles of sauces and that TCS foods are being cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There is observed to be single service articles and boxes that were not inverted or covered on the top of the cook line. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all single service articles are protected from contamination by being inverted or covered.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
These physical facilities were observed to be in need of repair:

1. FIRST REPEAT- Remove the protective covering off cooking equipment and coolers.
2. There is ice build-up on the walls and floor of the walk in freezer. Ensure that the ice is removed and the issue is repaired.

Ensure that physical facilities are repaired and maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The PIC is observed to not have allergen awareness training. It was discussed to make sure that there is always a CFPM on site who has completed their allergen awareness training at all times of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs who have completed their allergen training to cover all hours of operations.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.
